payload.claim: The pluralization branch `("" if count == 1 else "s")` is never exercised for `count == 1`; every test that reaches this line uses `count == 2` (two failures) or `count == 0` (the green path, which takes the other branch of the outer conditional entirely). Replacing the whole expression with the constant `"s"` (always plural) keeps every existing `test_regate.py` assertion green, since the only non-green case tested prints '2 new failures' either way, while a real single-failure run would wrongly print '1 new failures' instead of '1 new failure'.
